item.text: The bug is exactly where expected: the error string carries Rich markup tags, but it’s printed through whatever markup setting the caller’s console has. I’m reading that small region plus prompt tests now, then I’ll patch only source.

item.aggregated_output:
import io

from rich.console import Console
from rich.prompt import Confirm, IntPrompt, Prompt


def test_prompt_str():
    INPUT = "egg\nfoo"
    console = Console(file=io.StringIO())
    name = Prompt.ask(
        "what is your name",
        console=console,
        choices=["foo", "bar"],
        default="baz",
        stream=io.StringIO(INPUT),
    )
    assert name == "foo"
    expected = "what is your name [foo/bar] (baz): Please select one of the available options\nwhat is your name [foo/bar] (baz): "
    output = console.file.getvalue()
    print(repr(output))
    assert output == expected


def test_prompt_str_case_insensitive():
    INPUT = "egg\nFoO"
    console = Console(file=io.StringIO())
    name = Prompt.ask(
        "what is your name",
        console=console,
        choices=["foo", "bar"],
        default="baz",
        case_sensitive=False,
        stream=io.StringIO(INPUT),
    )
    assert name == "foo"
    expected = "what is your name [foo/bar] (baz): Please select one of the available options\nwhat is your name [foo/bar] (baz): "
    output = console.file.getvalue()
    print(repr(output))
    assert output == expected


def test_prompt_str_default():
    INPUT = ""
    console = Console(file=io.StringIO())
    name = Prompt.ask(
        "what is your name",
        console=console,
        default="Will",
        stream=io.StringIO(INPUT),
    )
    assert name == "Will"
    expected = "what is your name (Will): "
    output = console.file.getvalue()
    print(repr(output))
    assert output == expected


def test_prompt_int():
    INPUT = "foo\n100"
    console = Console(file=io.StringIO())
    number = IntPrompt.ask(
        "Enter a number",
        console=console,
        stream=io.StringIO(INPUT),
    )
    assert number == 100
    expected = "Enter a number: Please enter a valid integer number\nEnter a number: "
    output = console.file.getvalue()
    print(repr(output))
    assert output == expected


def test_prompt_confirm_no():
    INPUT = "foo\nNO\nn"
    console = Console(file=io.StringIO())
    answer = Confirm.ask(
        "continue",
        console=console,
        stream=io.StringIO(INPUT),
    )
    assert answer is False
    expected = "continue [y/n]: Please enter Y or N\ncontinue [y/n]: Please enter Y or N\ncontinue [y/n]: "
    output = console.file.getvalue()
    print(repr(output))
    assert output == expected


def test_prompt_confirm_yes():
    INPUT = "foo\nNO\ny"
    console = Console(file=io.StringIO())
    answer = Confirm.ask(
        "continue",
        console=console,
        stream=io.StringIO(INPUT),
    )
    assert answer is True
    expected = "continue [y/n]: Please enter Y or N\ncontinue [y/n]: Please enter Y or N\ncontinue [y/n]: "
    output = console.file.getvalue()
    print(repr(output))
    assert output == expected


def test_prompt_confirm_default():
    INPUT = "foo\nNO\ny"
    console = Console(file=io.StringIO())
    answer = Confirm.ask(
        "continue", console=console, stream=io.StringIO(INPUT), default=True
    )
    assert answer is True
    expected = "continue [y/n] (y): Please enter Y or N\ncontinue [y/n] (y): Please enter Y or N\ncontinue [y/n] (y): "
    output = console.file.getvalue()
    print(repr(output))
    assert output == expected

item.text:
Fixed the prompt validation error rendering in [rich/prompt.py](/Users/tapabratapal/Projects/provasign/research/harness/results/resolved-cases-native-2026-09-19/work/Textualize__rich__pr3882.r2.gpt55_native/rich/prompt.py:265). `PromptBase.on_validate_error()` now calls `self.console.print(error, markup=True)`, so `[prompt.invalid]` tags are interpreted even when the supplied console has `markup=False`.

Verified with:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/test_prompt.py
```

Also checked the direct `Confirm.ask(..., Console(markup=False))` reproduction; the output is now `Please enter Y or N` without the raw tag.
